title: Shanga settled
description: A Swahili trading community forms in the Lamu archipelago, with one of the earliest mosques found on the East African coast.

title: Gedi founded
description: A Swahili town of coral-stone houses, mosques and a palace begins to grow in the coastal forest, trading as far as China.

title: Ibn Battuta visits Mombasa
description: The Moroccan traveller spends a night in Mombasa on his voyage down the Swahili coast and describes its people and mosques.

title: Zheng He's fleet at Malindi
description: On its fifth voyage the Chinese treasure fleet sails down the East African coast as far as Malindi.

title: Vasco da Gama at Malindi
description: After a hostile reception at Mombasa the Portuguese fleet is welcomed at Malindi, where it takes on a pilot for the crossing to India.

title: Portuguese sack Mombasa
description: The fleet of Francisco de Almeida takes, loots and burns the city on its way to India.

title: Fort Jesus begun
description: Portugal builds a fortress at the harbour mouth to hold the Swahili coast, and it changes hands at least nine times in the next three centuries.

title: Fort Jesus falls to Oman
description: After a siege of nearly three years the Omanis take the fort, ending Portuguese power on the coast north of Mozambique.

title: Battle of Shela
description: The people of Lamu defeat an invasion from Pate and Mombasa and then ask Oman for protection, which brings Omani rule to the northern coast.

title: Said bin Sultan takes Mombasa
description: The ruler of Oman and Zanzibar removes the Mazrui governors of Mombasa and brings the whole coast under his control.

title: Mission founded at Rabai
description: Johann Ludwig Krapf and Johannes Rebmann set up a mission station inland from Mombasa, from which they travel into the interior.

title: Imperial British East Africa Company
description: A company chartered in London takes over the administration of the coast and the route to Uganda from the sultan of Zanzibar.

title: East Africa Protectorate proclaimed
description: The British government takes over from the failing company and rules the territory directly.

title: Nairobi founded
description: A depot on the Uganda Railway grows into a town that soon replaces Mombasa as the capital.

title: Railway reaches Lake Victoria
description: The line from Mombasa reaches the lake, opening the highlands to settlers and trade.

title: Koitalel arap Samoei killed
description: A British officer shoots the Nandi leader at a meeting, ending ten years of Nandi resistance to the railway.

title: Harry Thuku protest
description: Police fire on a crowd demanding the release of the nationalist Harry Thuku, killing at least 21 people.

title: State of emergency declared
description: The governor declares an emergency against the Mau Mau movement and has Jomo Kenyatta arrested, the start of years of war and mass detention.

title: Kenyatta convicted at Kapenguria
description: Jomo Kenyatta and five others are sentenced to seven years' hard labour for managing Mau Mau, a charge they deny.

title: Dedan Kimathi captured
description: The capture of the Mau Mau leader, who is hanged the following year, marks the end of the forest war.

title: Hola massacre
description: Guards club eleven detainees to death, and the outcry in Britain hastens the end of the emergency and of colonial rule.

title: Independence
description: Kenya becomes independent with Jomo Kenyatta as prime minister, and a republic exactly a year later.

title: Tom Mboya assassinated
description: The minister widely seen as a possible successor to Kenyatta is shot dead in the street, which deepens the division between Luo and Kikuyu.

title: Death of Jomo Kenyatta
description: The first president dies in office and is succeeded by Daniel arap Moi, who rules for 24 years.

title: Coup attempt
description: Air force men seize the radio station for some hours, and after their defeat Moi tightens one-party rule.

title: Saba Saba protests
description: Police break up a banned rally calling for multi-party democracy, which is restored the following year.

title: United States embassy bombing
description: An al-Qaeda truck bomb kills more than 200 people, nearly all of them Kenyans, minutes apart from an attack in Dar es Salaam.

title: Opposition wins the election
description: Mwai Kibaki defeats Moi's chosen successor, ending the rule of the party that had governed since independence.

title: Disputed election
description: Kibaki is declared re-elected over Raila Odinga, and more than a thousand people die in two months of violence that ends with a power-sharing agreement.

title: New constitution
description: A constitution approved by referendum limits the president's powers and creates 47 counties.

title: Westgate mall attack
description: Gunmen of al-Shabaab attack a shopping mall and kill 67 people in a siege lasting four days.

title: Supreme Court annuls the presidential election
description: Judges cancel Uhuru Kenyatta's re-election over irregularities and order a new vote, the first such ruling in Africa.
